skills.name: The hand lens and the microscope

note.text:
We study living things first with our five senses: sight, hearing, touch, smell (and taste only at home with food, never in the laboratory).
A hand lens magnifies a little (about five to ten times).
A compound light microscope magnifies much more. Its parts: eyepiece, objective lenses (on a turning nosepiece), stage with clips, mirror or lamp, coarse focus knob, fine focus knob, arm and base.
Total magnification = eyepiece magnification × objective magnification. With a ×10 eyepiece and a ×40 objective, the total is ×400.
The image under a microscope is upside down and the wrong way round.

worked_example.problem: A microscope has a ×{e} eyepiece and a ×{o} objective. What is the total magnification?

cards.idea: A microscope has an eyepiece, objective lenses, a stage, a mirror or lamp, focus knobs, an arm and a base.
example: You look through the eyepiece; the slide sits on the stage.

cards.idea: A hand lens magnifies a little; a microscope magnifies much more and shows cells.
example: A hand lens shows the hairs on a leaf; a microscope shows its cells.

pick.why: The eyepiece is the lens you look through.
The objective lenses are the lenses near the specimen; they give different magnifications.
The coarse focus knob moves the lenses a lot, to focus roughly.
The fine focus knob moves the lenses a little, to make the image sharp.
The mirror reflects light up through the specimen.
The arm is used to carry the microscope and holds the tube.
The base keeps the microscope steady.

questions.prompt: The total magnification is ×{magnification(e, o)} and the eyepiece is ×{e}. What is the magnification of the objective lens?

misconceptions.explain: Divide the total by the eyepiece magnification.

solution: Total = eyepiece × objective, so objective = total ÷ eyepiece.
